content:
luke-infra: kicking off terraform apply for release v2025.03 — infra changes limited to staging -> prod peering routes and a small IAM role addition for billing-sync. holding if deploybot shows any policy drift.

deploybot: preflight checks complete. plan shows 6 resources to add, 1 to update, 0 deletes. no provider version changes detected.
```# summary
+ aws_route.peering: 6 to add
~ aws_iam_role.billing-sync: update
```

maria-ops: @luke-infra quick Q — can we pin module versions for this apply? finance wants an explicit note in the release. last time a non-pinned module caused a subtle provider change.

luke-infra: yes, I'm applying with module_version_lockfile v2. See command below. if deploybot still flags provider drift I'll hold.
```terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -lockfile=module_lock.json
deploybot approve --preflight
```

raj-eng: pinging for the traffic-shift plan — network will shift 20% to new peering for 2 hours, then 100% if latency/err rates look fine. rollback plan: revert route add + remove new route target; run a staged apply to remove the newly added peering.

olivia-devex: dropping release notes link: https://docs.internal/release-notes/v2025.03 — include the IAM role change and peering details. Also add a prompt test for the billing-sync role in the canary testset.

deploybot: safety check: drift-detection hook found 1 out-of-band route on prod edge (extra cidr). marking apply HOLD, please ack and confirm remediation or proceed with --force.

luke-infra: ack. pushing a quick run to remove the stray cidr from the edge.
```# remediation
terraform apply -target=aws_route.edge_cleanup -auto-approve
```

maria-ops: if you remove it, confirm with @sre-bot that there are no active sessions relying on that cidr. we should capture a numbered rollback ticket before continuing.

sre-bot: verified: no active session metrics tied to that cidr in the last 30m. safe to remove. created incident ticket INF-4539 (rollback-ready).

luke-infra: remediation applied, re-running preflight.

deploybot: preflight OK. advancing to canary apply (az-a only) with traffic-shift 20% for 10m. will auto-mitigate to previous state on any >=5% error rate spike.

raj-eng: monitoring hooks enabled. will watch p50/p95 and errorrate on the next 15m window.

olivia-devex: tagging the release notes "infra: peering + billing-sync role" and adding rollout checklist item: confirm canary logs + run eval-prompt test.

deploybot: canary apply started at 1758457030.

luke-infra: seeing expected warmup. no errors so far.

deploybot: canary signals green after 600s. beginning traffic shift to 50% and scheduling full apply in 10m unless manual hold.

maria-ops: holding for 5m while finance signs off on IAM changes (they notified risk team). please don't proceed to 100% without explicit ok.

luke-infra: understood. pausing auto progression.

deploybot: auto-progression paused by manual hold (maria-ops). next action requires explicit 'deploybot continue' from maria-ops or luke-infra.

maria-ops: finance approved via email thread, INF-PR-77. deploybot continue. :thumbsup:

deploybot: full apply started at 1758457389. plan applied successfully. summary: 6 resources added, 1 updated. no rollbacks required.

luke-infra: thanks team. creating a short postmortem note in the release doc with the module_lock.json snapshot and the rollback ticket INF-4539 for traceability.

olivia-devex: noted — I'll add a blurb to the release notes and update the canary checklist with the deploybot flags we hit.

raj-eng: monitoring for 1h; will reopen if any anomalies.

maria-ops: closing the hold. good job everyone. :party_parrot:
